questions.question: What is another word for 'precipitate' (line 6)?
questions.explanation: In this context, precipitate means to throw or hurl something suddenly.

questions.question: Which of the following words is a synonym of 'proclivities' (line 19)?
questions.explanation: Proclivities are natural tendencies or inclinations.

questions.question: Which of the following is an antonym of ‘profusion’ (line5)?
questions.explanation: Profusion means a very large amount. Moderation means a limited or reasonable amount, so it is the opposite.

questions.question:
'took cognisance of fellow passengers' (line 10)
What is another way of saying ‘cognisance’?
questions.explanation: To take cognisance of something means to notice or pay attention to it.

questions.question:
'justifiable political aspirations' (line 1)
What is another way of saying 'justifiable'?
questions.explanation: Justifiable means reasonable, defensible or legitimate.

questions.question: What would be another word for 'eradicated' in line 27?
questions.explanation: Eradicated means completely removed or destroyed.

questions.question: What would be another word for 'piquant' in line 33?
questions.explanation: In this context, piquant means pleasantly interesting or stimulating.

questions.question: Which is the closest in meaning to 'wistful'? (line 9)
questions.explanation: Wistful means quietly thoughtful or longing, so dreamy is the closest choice.

questions.question: Which is closest in meaning to 'discreetly'? (line 44)
questions.explanation: Discreetly means carefully and without attracting attention; secretively is the closest option.

questions.question: Which of the words below means the same as ‘Providence’ (line 10)?
questions.explanation: Providence can mean a guiding power or fate.
